text:
[title] Speculative decoding
[body] A small draft model proposes gamma tokens
[body] The target model verifies them in one forward pass
[body] Rejection sampling keeps the output distribution exact

novice.takeaway: The slide explains a technique called speculative decoding where a small model quickly guesses several tokens, which a bigger model checks in one step, speeding things up without changing the final output.
questions: Why is it called 'gamma' tokens specifically?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe speculative decoding speeds up AI responses without sacrificing accuracy.

peer.takeaway: A small draft model proposes multiple tokens which a larger target model verifies at once, using rejection sampling to speed decoding without changing output distribution.
questions: What determines the value of gamma?
How much speedup does this give versus baseline decoding?
How does this combine with the block table technique?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe speculative decoding speeds up inference while preserving exact output correctness.

expert.takeaway: The slide summarizes the standard speculative decoding mechanism: draft model proposes tokens, target model verifies in parallel, rejection sampling preserves exact output distribution.
questions: What value of gamma was used in the system?
How does draft model choice affect acceptance rate?
What speedup does this contribute to the 2.4x figure?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to accept speculative decoding as a lossless speedup technique used in their system.
